4: Built-in mask mixin class.

6: The design uses `Masked` as a factory class which automatically

12: ``from_unmasked(data, mask, copy=False)`` class method that
13: creates an instance from unmasked data and a mask, as well as
14: the ``unmasked`` property that returns just the data.
15: The `Masked` class itself provides a base ``mask`` property,
16: which can also be overridden if needed.

52:         a subclass of the type of ``data``.
53:     mask : array-like of bool, optional
54:         The initial mask to assign.  If not given, taken from the data.
55:     copy : bool

58:     """

60:     _base_classes = {}

import numpy as np
from astropy import units as u
from astropy.utils.masked import Masked

# nansum expected value via function helper (method removed in 8.0.2)
q3 = np.array([1., 2., np.nan, 4.]) * u.m
initial = 0 * u.m
where = q3 < 4 * u.m
print("np.nansum(q, initial, where) =", np.nansum(q3, initial=initial, where=where))  # expect 3 m

# Masked where logic — verify expected values my tests assert
data = np.arange(6.).reshape(2,3)
mask = np.array([[True, False, False],[False, True, False]])
ma = Masked(data, mask=mask)
where = np.array([[True, False, False],[True, True, True]])
where_final = ~ma.mask & where
for axis in (0, 1, None):
    r = ma.mean(axis, where=where)
    e_d = ma.unmasked.mean(axis, where=where_final)
    e_m = np.logical_or.reduce(ma.mask, axis=axis, where=where_final) | (~where_final).all(axis)
    ok_d = np.array_equal(r.unmasked, e_d, equal_nan=True)
    ok_m = np.array_equal(r.mask, e_m)
    print(f"mean axis={axis}: data_ok={ok_d} mask_ok={ok_m} -> {r.unmasked} {r.mask}")

    rv = ma.var(axis, where=where)
    ev_d = ma.unmasked.var(axis, where=where_final)
    print(f"var  axis={axis}: data_ok={np.allclose(rv.unmasked, ev_d, equal_nan=True)} -> {rv.unmasked} {rv.mask}")

    rs = ma.std(axis, where=where)
    es_d = ma.unmasked.std(axis, where=where_final)
    print(f"std  axis={axis}: data_ok={np.allclose(rs.unmasked, es_d, equal_nan=True)} -> {rs.unmasked} {rs.mask}")

    ma_eq = ma == ma
    ra = ma_eq.any(axis, where=where)
    ea_d = ma_eq.unmasked.any(axis, where=where_final)
    ea_m = np.logical_or.reduce(ma.mask, axis=axis, where=where_final) | (~where_final).all(axis)
    print(f"any  axis={axis}: data_ok={np.array_equal(ra.unmasked, ea_d)} mask_ok={np.array_equal(ra.mask, ea_m)}")
    rl = ma_eq.all(axis, where=where)
    el_d = ma_eq.unmasked.all(axis, where=where_final)
    print(f"all  axis={axis}: data_ok={np.array_equal(rl.unmasked, el_d)} mask_ok={np.array_equal(rl.mask, ea_m)}")
    print()
"}
